place.name: Warorot Market (Kad Luang)
place.thai: ตลาดวโรรส (กาดหลวง)
knownFor: Oldest big market of Chiang Mai; market since 1910 (Princess Dara Rasmi)
Northern Thai packaged foods to bring home: sai ua, nam phrik num, khaep mu, moo yor
Dry goods, chili pastes, banana-leaf sweets; upper floors fabric, hill-tribe clothing, indigo cloth, temple bells
Part of the Chinatown (Trok Lao Jo) district

signatureFoods.th: น้ำพริกหนุ่ม

signatureFoods.en: pork cracklings (eaten with nam phrik num)
fried pork (Dam Rong / ดำรงค์ stall known for this)

signatureFoods.th: มะปรางอ่อน
signatureFoods.en: young marian plum, very sour, dipped in chili-shrimp paste

dishes.name: khao soi
dishes.description: Egg noodles in coconut-milk curry broth, topped with crispy fried noodles; served with pickled mustard greens, shallots, lime, chilli. CMU notes it is associated with Chinese Muslim (Chin Haw / Ho) cooks.
ingredients: curry paste (dried chilli, turmeric, kaffir lime rind)

dishes.name: sai ua
dishes.description: Coiled pork sausage packed with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaf, galangal, turmeric, chilli, shallot; grilled or smoked. Popular Chiang Mai souvenir.

dishes.thai: น้ำพริกหนุ่ม
dishes.name: nam phrik num
dishes.description: Pounded roasted long green chillies, garlic and shallots; eaten with sticky rice, pork crackling (khaep mu) and vegetables. Can be very hot.

dishes.thai: น้ำพริกอ่อง
dishes.name: nam phrik ong
dishes.description: Bolognese-like relish of minced pork, tomato and dried chilli; mild; served with raw/boiled vegetables and pork crackling.

dishes.name: kaeng hang le
dishes.description: Rich, oily pork curry using dried spice mix (hang le powder), ginger, tamarind, pickled garlic, sometimes peanuts; eaten with ordinary rice rather than sticky rice. Name from Burmese 'hin lay'.

dishes.name: kaeng khae
dishes.description: Coconut-free curry of many local vegetables and herbs (phak khae, cha-om, pea eggplant, bamboo, ivy gourd, dried kapok flower) with chicken, frog, dried fish or snail.

dishes.name: kaeng ho
dishes.description: 'Ho' = put together: leftover curries (esp. hang le) stir-fried with glass noodles, pickled bamboo, vegetables and kaffir lime leaves; often made after festivals.

dishes.name: larb mueang
dishes.description: Minced pork (or beef/buffalo) with blood, offal and a dry spice paste (makhwaen, long pepper, cloves, etc.) — darker and drier than Isan larb; eaten raw ('dip') or cooked ('khua'). Served with bitter/fragrant side greens.

dishes.name: larb nuea
dishes.description: Spicy chopped beef with local herbs, galangal and makhwaen to cut gaminess.

dishes.thai: ขนมจีนน้ำเงี้ยว
dishes.name: khanom chin nam ngiao
dishes.english: rice noodles with Shan-style pork-tomato broth
dishes.description: Fermented rice noodles in a tangy tomato-pork rib broth with blood cake, thua nao and dried kapok flower (dok ngiu); Tai Yai (Shan) origin; auspicious banquet dish in Lanna.

dishes.name: khaep mu
dishes.description: Crispy deep-fried pork skin; eaten with nam phrik num/ong. Chiang Mai souvenir.

dishes.name: naem
dishes.description: Pork mixed with garlic, salt and sticky rice, wrapped in banana leaves and fermented 2-3 days; eaten raw, grilled in leaf (jin som mok) or stir-fried with egg.

dishes.thai: ข้าวกั๊นจิ๊น
dishes.name: khao kan jin
dishes.description: Rice mixed with minced pork and pork blood, seasoned, steamed in banana leaf; topped with fried garlic and dried chilli. Tai Yai origin; 'kan' squeeze, 'jin' meat.

dishes.name: tam khanun
dishes.description: Boiled young jackfruit pounded with chilli paste then stir-fried with pork, garlic, tomato and kaffir lime leaf; topped with fried garlic and chilli.

dishes.name: kaeng khanun
dishes.description: Green jackfruit curry with pork ribs, tomato, cha-om and pepper vine; auspicious name so served at weddings and New Year.

dishes.thai: แกงผักหวานใส่ไข่มด
dishes.name: kaeng phak wan sai khai mot
dishes.english: wild sweet-leaf soup with red ant eggs
dishes.description: Light curry-soup of phak wan pa leaves and red ant eggs with tomato; prized for its 'popping' texture; eaten hot with sticky rice.

dishes.name: chio khai mot daeng
dishes.description: Red ant eggs cooked in a chilli-shallot-tomato broth with beaten egg stirred in; also called chio khai mot som.

dishes.thai: แกงผักชะอม
dishes.thaiNorthern: แก๋งผักหละ
dishes.name: kaeng phak cha-om
dishes.description: Simple Northern vegetable curry of cha-om with dried fish, young galangal and roasted green chilli.

dishes.thai: ไข่เจียวชะอม
dishes.name: khai chiao cha-om
dishes.description: Thick omelette packed with cha-om shoots; national rather than specifically Lanna, sold at curry-rice stalls; often cut into squares and eaten with nam phrik kapi or in kaeng som.

dishes.name: yam phak kut
dishes.description: Blanched fern fronds tossed with pork/shrimp, shallot, chilli, lime, sometimes coconut cream.

dishes.thai: แกงเห็ดถอบ
dishes.thaiNorthern: แก๋งเห็ดถอบ
dishes.name: kaeng het thop
dishes.description: Het thop / het pho with pickled bamboo shoots and chicken or pork in chilli paste broth; the signature early-rains dish.

dishes.thai: แกงเห็ดตับเต่า
dishes.name: kaeng het tap tao
dishes.description: Bolete mushrooms with minced pork and young tamarind leaves (or acidum) in chilli broth.

dishes.name: kaeng het lom
dishes.description: Het lom mushrooms with cha-om and pepper-vine leaves, galangal and lemongrass.

dishes.thai: แกงหน่อไม้
dishes.name: kaeng no mai
dishes.description: Fresh bamboo shoots with cha-om, pepper vine and yanang leaves; sometimes pork bones, fish or crab paste.

dishes.name: jo phak kat
dishes.description: Flowering mustard greens boiled with shrimp paste or fermented fish, soured with tamarind, often with pork ribs; topped with dried chilli and fried garlic.

dishes.name: khai pam
dishes.description: Beaten eggs with spring onion and chilli poured into banana-leaf cups and grilled over charcoal; variants add pork, fish or crab.

dishes.name: pu ong
dishes.english: rice-field crab fat grilled in shell
dishes.description: Crab fat/roe mixed with egg and seasoning, grilled in the crab shell.

dishes.name: tam som o
dishes.description: Pomelo pounded with garlic, lemongrass and nam pu (crab paste).

dishes.name: kaeng bon
dishes.description: Araceae (taro) stems steamed until soft (to remove itchiness) and cooked with pork ears, tamarind and spices; also cooked in bamboo as 'lam bon'.

dishes.thai: แกงผักเชียงดา
dishes.name: kaeng phak chiang da
dishes.description: Tender phak chiang da leaves with dried fish and cherry tomato in chilli broth; sometimes with cha-om.

dishes.name: khua pham
dishes.description: Pham (khai nam) stir-fried with pork belly, lemongrass, galangal and kaffir lime leaf.

dishes.name: miang
dishes.description: Fermented tea leaves chewed after meals, sometimes wrapped with salt, ginger, coconut, peanuts (miang song-khrueang); social snack.

dishes.thai: ไก่ทอดมะแขว่น
dishes.name: kai thot makhwaen
dishes.description: Chicken marinated with makhwaen pepper and fried; eaten with sticky rice.

dishes.thai: น้ำพริกน้ำปู
dishes.name: nam phrik nam pu
dishes.description: Relish based on black rice-field crab paste (nam pu) with chilli.

dishes.name: ho nueng
dishes.description: Chicken, pork, fish or bamboo shoot with curry paste steamed in banana leaf.

words.thai: สะหวัดดีเจ้า
words.note: Women end with jao (เจ้า); men use khap (คับ). Also spelled สวั๋สดีเจ้า.

words.thai: สะหวัดดีคับ

words.note: Male polite form.
Key false friend: in Central Thai ยินดี means 'glad / you're welcome'; in Kham Mueang it is the everyday 'thank you'. Men: ยินดีคับ.

Answering just 'jao' means 'yes (politely)'. Men use khap.
Also written คั่บ.
Vendor agreeing to a request.

words.thai: บ่ะได้เจ้า
words.note: Vendor declining (e.g. a discount).

words.thai: บ่ะเอาเจ้า
words.note: Polite way to decline an offer. Centara: BOR-AO.
Also intensifier: ลำแต๊ๆ = really delicious. Spelled แต้ in some sources.

words.centralThai: สนุก / ไพเราะ
words.note: Very common positive word.

words.thai: อู้กำเมือง
words.centralThai: พูดภาษาเหนือ
words.note: Locals appreciate even a few words. คำเมือง is also spelled กำเมือง.
Ambiguous: sources list it for both 1st and 3rd person. LLM should resolve from context.
In Central Thai ข้า sounds archaic/rude; register differs. Needs review.

words.english: you (formal) - same word as the polite particle

words.note: Informal; do not use with strangers or elders.
Impolite outside close friends; translation should flag rudeness.
ญ is pronounced as a palatal nasal (ny).
Also written บ่อ / บ่ะ / หมะ. Most important negation word.
e.g. ได้ก่อ = can (you)?

words.centralThai: หรือ / เหรอ
words.note: e.g. มาเมินแล้วกา = been here long?

words.centralThai: ใช่ไหม / เหรอ
words.note: ใช่ก่อ / ใช่ก๊ะ = isn't it?
As in สบายดีบ๋อ. Distinguish from negative บ่ by tone/position (final).

words.centralThai: (คำลงท้ายคำสั่ง)
words.note: Wikipedia classes it as authoritative imperative; tone may sound bossy.

words.centralThai: หน่อย / ด้วย
words.note: Wikipedia: polite request particle. Central equivalent approximate.
ไปเฮียนกันเต๊อะ = let's go study.
เอา...แหม = another one. Not the Central exclamation แหม.
ลำขนาด = very delicious; งามขนาด = very pretty.
จ๊าดลำ = really delicious.
เก็บตังค์ตวยเจ้า = the bill please.
Pointing at goods further away.
Also short หยัง; หยัง can also mean 'why/how come'.

words.centralThai: อะไร / ทำไม
words.note: วันนี้หยังมางาม = why so pretty today (compliment).

Compiler: krunuttaya (see regional_dialects.json) lists บะก้วย as the Chiang Mai form and บะแก๋ว/บะมั้น as other-province forms; trueplookpanya gives บะหมั้น without a province. Accept all forms; expert to confirm.

months.air: Haze season underway; open-burning ban in force (Chiang Mai 2026 ban: 1 Jan-31 May). PM2.5 often above Thai 24h standard (37.5 ug/m3). Cold-air inversions trap smoke in the valley.
months.talk: Cool mornings (often ~15C, colder in the hills) - locals remark it is cold (หนาว, nao) and wear jackets; peak tourist/flower season; smoke starting to be mentioned.

months.season: cool -> hot (TMD: hot season from mid-Feb)
months.air: Haze worsening; agricultural and forest burning. Chiang Mai 2021 monthly mean PM2.5 47.7 ug/m3 (IQAir).
months.talk: Days warming fast, dry; talk turns to ฝุ่น (fun, dust/PM2.5) and masks, checking AQI apps; burning ban.

months.air: Usually the WORST month for smoke. Chiang Mai 2021 monthly mean PM2.5 83.3 ug/m3 (IQAir); late March 2026 hit purple alert level. Visibility of Doi Suthep often lost.
months.talk: Hottest-and-smokiest stretch: ฝุ่นควัน (fun khwan, dust-smoke) and ไฟป่า (fai pa, forest fires) dominate small talk; masks, air purifiers, people leaving town; 'ฮ้อน' (hon, Kham Mueang for hot).

months.air: Smoke typically persists into April until pre-monsoon storms clear the air; varies by year.
months.talk: Peak heat (avg high ~37C). 'ฮ้อนใบ้ฮ้อนง่าว' (hon bai hon ngao, 'extremely hot' in Kham Mueang). Pi Mai Mueang / Songkran water festival 13-15 April falls in Lanna month 7 (เดือนเจ็ด) = Lanna New Year; water-throwing offers relief from heat.

months.season: hot -> rainy (TMD: rainy season from mid-May)
months.air: Air usually improves as rains begin; burning-control period can still be in force (to 31 May in 2026).
months.talk: First storms; relief from heat and smoke. Hed thop / hed phao (เห็ดถอบ / เห็ดเผาะ, earthstar mushrooms) appear at markets and roadsides after alternating rain and heat, sold by the litre at high prices early in season. Inthakhin city-pillar festival (late May-early June).

months.air: Generally clean air (rain washes out particulates).
months.talk: Rainy season settling in; rice planting in valleys; afternoon/evening downpours; talk about getting caught in rain on motorbikes.
Rainy; Buddhist Lent (Khao Phansa) begins around the July full moon. Green season, fewer tourists.
Wettest month (~223 mm, ~17 rain days). Flood watch on the Ping River begins; mushrooms, bamboo shoots and wild greens in markets.
Very wet; flood risk from Ping River (major floods have peaked late Sep-early Oct). Humidity ~82%.

months.season: rainy -> cool (TMD: cool season from mid-Oct)
months.talk: Rains tapering; Ping River flood peaks historically early October (2011: +4.95 m; 2022: +4.75 m; 2024: +5.30 m on 5 Oct at Nawarat Bridge gauge). Lanna month 1 = เดือนเกี๋ยง (duean kiang); Salak Phat merit-making; end of Lent (Ok Phansa).

months.air: Generally good; occasional early haze as the dry season starts.
months.talk: Cool, dry and pleasant; Yi Peng (ยี่เป็ง) = full moon of Lanna month 2 (เดือนยี่), coinciding with Loi Krathong (full moon of Central Thai month 12). Lanterns, krathong; very busy.

months.air: Air quality begins to decline in the dry season; PM2.5 can exceed standards on still, cool mornings.
months.talk: Coolest nights (avg low ~17C, record 3.8C); locals bundle up, hot soups; high tourist season; talk of mountain trips for the cold.

festivals.name: Bo Sang Umbrella and San Kamphaeng Crafts Festival
festivals.thai: เทศกาลร่มบ่อสร้างและหัตถกรรมสันกำแพง
festivals.what: Craft festival of the paper/cotton umbrella-making village: umbrella-painting and paper-making demonstrations, craft workshops, a local 'kad mueang' market with local food, a parade decorated with umbrellas and traditional dancers.

festivals.name: Chiang Mai Flower Festival
festivals.thai: มหกรรมไม้ดอกไม้ประดับจังหวัดเชียงใหม่
festivals.what: Flower-float parade (Saturday), flower exhibitions and competitions, Miss Flower Festival pageant, plant market. Featured flowers include chrysanthemums and damask roses.

festivals.name: Poy Sang Long (Shan / Tai Yai novice ordination)
festivals.thai: ปอยส่างลอง
festivals.what: Three-day ceremony: boys (about 7-14) have heads shaved, are dressed as princes (sang long) in imitation of Prince Siddhartha, carried on relatives' shoulders so their feet do not touch the ground, paraded to temples, and ordained as novices on day three.

festivals.name: Inthakhin City Pillar Festival (Sai Khan Dok)
festivals.thai: ประเพณีใส่ขันดอกบูชาเสาอินทขิล
festivals.what: Chiang Mai people bring khan dok (bowls/cones of flowers), incense and candles to honour the city pillar for the city's stability and prosperity at the start of the rainy season; opening procession of the Phra Chao Saen Ha Buddha image; temple fair runs morning to midnight.

festivals.name: Tan Kuay Salak (lot-drawn alms baskets)
festivals.thai: ประเพณีตานก๋วยสลาก
festivals.what: Families prepare kuay salak (woven bamboo baskets) of food and daily necessities, write a salak slip naming a deceased relative, and monks draw lots to receive baskets; merit goes to the dead and goods help monks and the poor. Big decorated 'kuay chok' baskets may hold mirrors, combs, umbrellas.

festivals.name: Salak Yom (Lamphun)
festivals.thai: ประเพณีสลากย้อม
festivals.what: Unique Lamphun tradition with roots in the Yong people (related to the Tai Lue of Sipsongpanna): unmarried young women make and offer tall decorated salak trees (3-12 m) hung with offerings; believed to earn merit comparable to a man's ordination. Nightly lights and a procession of salak trees.

festivals.name: Wan Phra (Buddhist holy days)
festivals.thai: วันพระ
festivals.what: Observance days: devout people go to the temple, keep precepts; some eat vegetarian. Not an alcohol-ban day by law (only the five major Buddhist days are).

festivals.name: Yi Peng / Loy Krathong (Chiang Mai)
festivals.thai: ประเพณีเดือนยี่เป็ง / ลอยกระทง
festivals.what: Lanna festival of light held with Loy Krathong: temples and homes decorated with hanging and decorative paper lanterns (khom khwaen, khom fai), small clay oil lamps (phang prathip) lit as offerings, krathong floated on the Ping River, krathong procession/competition (2026: on 25 Nov). Sky lanterns (khom loi) are associated with the festival but the municipality asks that none be released inside Chiang Mai city; mass releases happen only at ticketed, permitted events outside the city.

festivals.name: Chinese New Year (Trut Chin)
festivals.thai: ตรุษจีน
festivals.what: Thai-Chinese families make offerings to ancestors and deities, give red envelopes (ang pao), shops may close for a day or two; lion/dragon dances around Chinatown.

festivals.name: Makha Bucha
festivals.thai: วันมาฆบูชา
festivals.what: Commemorates the assembly of 1,250 disciples. Morning merit-making, sermons, and evening candle-lit circumambulation of the temple hall (wian thian) three times.

festivals.name: Poy Sang Long (Shan / Tai Yai novice ordination)
festivals.thai: ปอยส่างลอง
festivals.what: Three-day ceremony: boys (about 7-14) have heads shaved, are dressed as princes (sang long) in imitation of Prince Siddhartha, carried on relatives' shoulders so their feet do not touch the ground, paraded to temples, and ordained as novices on day three.

festivals.name: Songkran / Pi Mai Mueang (Lanna New Year)
festivals.thai: ป๋าเวณีปี๋ใหม่เมือง / สงกรานต์
festivals.what: Wan Sangkhan Long (สังขานต์ล่อง): old year leaves; firecrackers at dawn to drive off bad luck, house cleaning, bathing, new clothes. Wan Nao (วันเนา/วันเน่า): preparation day; do not quarrel or speak rudely or you will have bad luck all year; carry sand to temples and build sand chedis decorated with tung (paper/cloth flags). Wan Phaya Wan (วันพญาวัน): the true New Year; merit-making, bathing Buddha images, dam hua (ดำหัว) of elders - offering scented water with turmeric and som poi (ส้มป่อย), flowers, candles, asking forgiveness and receiving blessings; ไม้ค้ำศรี (bodhi-tree supports) offered. Wan Pak Pi (วันปากปี): start of the year; protective rites and destiny-extending candles.

festivals.name: Visakha Bucha
festivals.thai: วันวิสาขบูชา
festivals.what: Commemorates the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and passing. Merit-making, sermons and evening candle procession (wian thian).

festivals.name: Inthakhin City Pillar Festival (Sai Khan Dok)
festivals.thai: ประเพณีใส่ขันดอกบูชาเสาอินทขิล
festivals.what: Chiang Mai people bring khan dok (bowls/cones of flowers), incense and candles to honour the city pillar for the city's stability and prosperity at the start of the rainy season; opening procession of the Phra Chao Saen Ha Buddha image; temple fair runs morning to midnight.

festivals.name: Asalha Bucha and Khao Phansa (Start of Buddhist Lent)
festivals.thai: วันอาสาฬหบูชา / วันเข้าพรรษา
festivals.what: Asalha Bucha marks the first sermon. Khao Phansa begins the 3-month rains retreat: people give candles (hae thian phansa) and bathing cloths to monks; many Thais give up alcohol or other habits for Lent.
